critique:
field placed, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Same fact as before (the colors of the cubes put into the bin so far, oldest first, one entry per held-then-released execution), but the value form changes so that no quoting can go wrong: the value is the color words separated by single spaces with no brackets, quotes or commas, and the word none when nothing has been placed. Append the held cube's color at the decision step that directly follows an execution whose frames show a cube held and then released over the bin and whose scene shows the gripper fully open with nothing held; never after a pick-up or after the button. Example sequence: none -> none -> red -> red -> red red. e.g. blue blue blue green

field arrivals, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes currently lying on the table, in the order they first appeared in the episode, oldest first. Cubes of the goal colors are not all present at the start: new ones appear on the table while the robot works, and the oracle always picks, within the color being worked, the one that has been on the table longest. At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene (any order among those present at t=0, ordered by y as reported). At each later step: remove the entry of the cube the robot picked up during the step (the cube whose position matches where the fingers closed); append, at the end, every goal-color detection that is on the table in the scene at the decision step and matches no existing entry within about 12 px, except bin echoes (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) and release echoes (a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper when the fingers opened); refresh each remaining entry to its position in the scene at the decision step. The annotator may use the whole episode to check which detections are real cubes (a real one is later picked or stays at the same place for the rest of the episode). e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]

field placed, POLICY PROMPT
  Colors of the cubes put into the bin so far, oldest first, written as plain color words separated by single spaces, nothing else: no brackets, no quotes, no commas. Write the word none at the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames). Otherwise copy the carried-in value and, when an execution frame of this step has an object line ending 'is held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step (the last frame) shows the fingers about 100% open with no held line, append one space and that cube's color (if the carried-in value is none, replace it by the color). Gripper position at release, partial openings in intermediate frames and same-color detections popping up near the bin do not matter. Do not append when the last frame still shows a held cube, when there are no execution frames, or when the robot only pressed the button. e.g. carried-in red becomes red red; carried-in none after a released blue becomes blue

field arrivals, POLICY PROMPT
  Ordered list of [y, x] positions of the goal-color cubes lying on the table, oldest-arrived first; the policy picks the first entry of the color it is working. At the first decision step list every goal-color cube in the scene, in the order reported (by y). At every later step start from the carried-in list and apply, in order: (1) if an execution frame shows a cube held in the gripper, remove the entry closest to the gripper position in the frame where the fingers first closed (within about 12 px); (2) drop any entry that matches no table detection of its color in the last frame within about 12 px in two or more consecutive frames (the cube is gone); (3) append, at the end, each goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px, unless it is a bin echo (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) or a release echo (the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper at the frame the fingers opened); (4) update each remaining entry to its last-frame position. Write the list as nested brackets exactly like the example. e.g. [[70, 82], [95, 158], [79, 88]]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Three parts of the pick rule (Rule 3) sent the policy wrong; Rules 1 and 2 stood in every reported step and stay as they are, except that they must read `placed` in its new form (space-separated color words, none when empty) and count words per color. Color choice was wrong. The goal with two colors is not worked in the order the instruction names the colors: when the goal asked for one blue and two green cubes the oracle took green first, both greens, and the blue last; when it asked for three blue and two green it took the blues first. The rule that stands in place of 'first color in the goal instruction's order': work the color with the largest required count first, finish it entirely, then the next-largest; break a tie in required count by goal order. A color whose count in `placed` meets its requirement is finished and never picked again. There is no situation in this batch where the first-ordered color has no candidate, so the clause about moving on to another color when the preferred color has no valid cube should not be added. The candidate filter was wrong in two opposite ways. First, 'a detection that first appears during the step is not a candidate' must be removed: new cubes of the goal colors genuinely appear on the table while the robot works (in most episodes the scene opens with a single cube and the next ones appear during the first execution), and the oracle later picks them. Second, the bin-echo radius of 'about 35 px' was too large: a cube 30-35 px from the bin's reported center that sits at the same place in every frame is a real table cube and was picked; the detections that are echoes of bin contents lie about 25-26 px from the center. The filter that stands: exclude a detection within about 28 px of the bin's reported center, and exclude a detection of the just-released color that appears within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper in the frame where the fingers opened (the dropped cube seen beside the bin), unless that same detection was already present at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. Both exclusions apply at step #1 too. A detection that wobbles a few px between frames while the arm passes near it is still a candidate. The ordering among candidates was wrong. 'Nearest the bin' and the 'larger y' tie-break each contradicted recorded picks. What the recorded picks follow is age: within the color being worked, the oracle picks the cube that has been on the table longest, and that is the first entry of that color in the new memory field `arrivals`. The rule that stands in place of the distance preference and the larger-y tie-break: among candidates of the working color, choose the one that is first in `arrivals` (match entries to last-frame detections within about 12 px). Only when several candidates are tied in `arrivals` (all present since the start of the episode) fall back to the one nearest the bin's reported center that is not excluded above. Point at the candidate's center as reported in the last frame; within about 3 px is correct. Remove the sentence about preferring the larger y when two candidates are within 5 px of the same bin distance, and the sentence that a candidate must be at nearly the same place in all but one execution frame. The fallback paragraph stays, but its 'stable cube nearest the bin' should read 'first `arrivals` entry of a needed color, else nearest the bin'.

refused
  Every memory report in this batch says the same thing: the policy appended the right color but wrote the list with single quotes instead of the double-quoted JSON form the instruction demanded, and the policy itself says nothing was missing from the instruction. Those reports are not passed on as instruction gaps; instead the field's form is changed to plain space-separated words so there is no quoting to get wrong, which is the only thing that actually stops this slip. The several tie-break proposals for choosing among cubes of the needed color are not passed on as stated: one step proposed preferring the smaller x, one the cube farthest from the bin, two the cube nearest the gripper or with the smaller y, one the cube nearest the bin after discarding everything within 40 px; each fits the single step that proposed it and contradicts other recorded picks in the same batch (one episode picks the farthest-from-bin cube at one step and the nearest-to-bin cube at the next). What the picks do follow across episodes is arrival order, which is what the new `arrivals` field carries. Among cubes that were all present from the very start of an episode the recorded order is not settled by anything observed, so no geometric tie-break is claimed to be correct there; nearest-to-bin is kept only as a fallback. The proposal that a detection present at a fixed position in every frame is a real cube regardless of its distance to the bin is also refused: detections about 25-26 px from the bin's center stay fixed for the whole episode and are never picked, so the bin-echo exclusion stays, only with a smaller radius.
